title: Connectedness and Orthogonality of Block Designs
breadcrumb: Unit III · Design of Experiments · Block-design structure
objectives: Define connectedness of a block design in terms of estimable treatment contrasts.
Use the treatment concurrence graph to reason about connectedness.
Interpret the information matrix C=R−NK⁻¹N′ and the rank condition rank(C)=v−1.
Explain orthogonality of treatment and block contrasts in complete block and Latin-square layouts.

traps: Connectedness means every treatment contrast is estimable after eliminating block effects; it is not the same as equal pair concurrence.
For a design with v treatments, rank(C)=v−1 is the connectedness condition when C=R−NK⁻¹N′.
A disconnected design can still estimate contrasts within each connected component, but not all contrasts across components.
A connected design need not be a BIBD; connectedness is about estimability, balance is about equal replication/concurrence.
Orthogonality means the relevant centred contrast cross-products are zero; it is not synonymous with connectedness.
In a complete RBD, every treatment occurs once in each block, making treatment and block contrasts orthogonal.
In a Latin square, treatment contrasts are orthogonal to both row and column contrasts under the standard balanced layout.
howto: For connectedness, construct a treatment graph: join two treatments if they occur together in a block. If the graph is connected, treatment contrasts are estimable; equivalently check rank(C)=v−1 for C=R−NK⁻¹N′. For orthogonality, identify the centred treatment and block contrast columns and check their cross-products are zero in the balanced layout.

Latin square: treatment contrasts are orthogonal to row and column contrasts.

scenes.title: Why connectedness matters
scenes.objective: Motivate estimability in incomplete block designs.
body: In an incomplete block design, not every treatment appears in every block. The block effects may absorb some treatment comparisons, so the key question is whether treatment contrasts can still be estimated after adjusting for blocks.
A design is connected when every treatment contrast is estimable. Connectedness is about information and estimability, not necessarily equal pair concurrence.

items.ask: What does connectedness guarantee in a block design?
items.recall: All independent treatment contrasts are estimable after adjusting for block effects.
refresh: There are v−1 independent treatment contrasts.
Some pairs may never share a block, yet paths through other treatments can connect them.

Connectedness is distinct from BIBD balance.  This rebuild makes the prerequisite explicit before the new design method is used. Identify what is being counted, which units are independent, and which assumptions allow the calculation. Then explain how that idea supports the next step rather than memorising the symbol alone.

items.recall: A linear comparison of treatment effects whose coefficients sum to zero.
refresh: With v treatments there are v−1 independent treatment contrasts.
Connectedness asks whether those contrasts can be estimated after eliminating block effects.
The grand-mean direction is not a treatment contrast and explains why the rank target is v−1.
A connectedness graph can provide an intuitive check before using the information matrix.

items.recall: The relevant centred contrast spaces have zero cross-products.
refresh: Orthogonality means the information for one effect is not entangled with the other effect in the balanced layout.
It can be checked through zero cross-products of centred design columns.
A complete RBD separates treatment and block contrasts; a Latin square separates treatment from row and column contrasts.
Orthogonality is different from connectedness, which is an estimability condition.

ask.nudge: State the rule in your own words, then connect it to the calculation or design example in this scene.

scenes.title: The treatment concurrence graph
scenes.objective: Translate block incidence into a graph.
body: Construct a graph with one vertex for each treatment. Join two vertices when the corresponding treatments occur together in at least one block.
If the graph has one connected component, any treatment can be linked to every other through a chain of shared-block comparisons. This is the graph interpretation of connectedness.

scenario.title: A chain connects four treatments
body: The concurrence graph has edges 1–2, 2–3 and 3–4. Treatments 1 and 4 never occur in the same block, but a path connects them.
Thus the graph is connected even though not every pair is directly adjacent.

A concurrence graph answers whether treatment comparisons can be linked through shared blocks. The information-matrix rank gives the algebraic version of that question. Orthogonality is separate: it concerns zero cross-products between centred contrast spaces. A design may be connected without equal pair concurrence, and connectedness alone does not establish orthogonality.
scenario.answer: Yes. The path 1–2–3–4 connects all four treatments.

ask.q: Must every pair of treatments share a block for the design to be connected?
ask.nudge: A path through intermediate treatments is enough.

blocks.body: A graph is connected if a path exists between every pair of vertices. A design with a connected concurrence graph is connected.
If the graph splits into components, comparisons between treatments in different components are not estimable after eliminating block effects.
Contrasts within a connected component may still be estimable. The failure concerns comparisons across disconnected components.

ask.q: If treatments form two separate concurrence-graph components, can a contrast comparing one treatment from each component be estimated?
ask.nudge: There is no chain of shared-block comparisons across the components.

scenes.answer: The design is disconnected; cross-component treatment contrasts are not estimable.

ask.nudge: One component contains 1,2,3; the other contains 4,5.

blocks.body: Let N be the v×b treatment-by-block incidence matrix. R is the diagonal matrix of treatment replications and K is the diagonal matrix of block sizes.
The adjusted treatment information matrix is C=R−NK⁻¹N′. It measures treatment information after accounting for block effects.
If every block has size k, then K=kI and C=R−(1/k)NN′. The matrix is singular in the overall-mean direction.

ask.q: What is the dimension of C when there are v treatments?

blocks.body: For a design with v treatments, rank(C)=v−1 if and only if all v−1 independent treatment contrasts are estimable.
Adding a common constant to all treatment effects does not change treatment contrasts. The grand-mean direction is therefore not part of the contrast information.
If there are c connected components, the rank is v−c under the standard incidence model; each component contributes one unidentifiable level shift.

scenes.title: A BIBD is connected when λ is positive
body: In a BIBD, every distinct treatment pair occurs together λ times. If λ>0, every pair is directly joined in the concurrence graph, so the graph is complete and connected.
This is a sufficient property of a BIBD, not a definition of connectedness. A connected design can have many pairs that never occur together directly.

scenario.teaser: A BIBD has v=4 and λ=1.
scenario.title: Every pair is adjacent
body: Every pair of treatments occurs together once. The concurrence graph is complete on four vertices.
It is therefore connected. A chain-connected design does not need this stronger all-pairs property.

A concurrence graph answers whether treatment comparisons can be linked through shared blocks. The information-matrix rank gives the algebraic version of that question. Orthogonality is separate: it concerns zero cross-products between centred contrast spaces. A design may be connected without equal pair concurrence, and connectedness alone does not establish orthogonality.
scenario.q: Is a BIBD with λ=1 connected?
scenario.answer: Yes. Every treatment pair shares a block.

ask.q: Does connectedness require λ to be constant across all pairs?
ask.nudge: No; it requires paths, not equal concurrence.

blocks.body: Two sets of effects are orthogonal when their centred design-contrast columns have zero cross-products. Their information can be separated without one effect's estimate depending on the other.
In a complete RBD, each treatment appears once in every block, so treatment contrasts are orthogonal to block contrasts.
Orthogonality concerns cross-products between effect spaces. Connectedness concerns whether treatment contrasts are estimable at all.

ask.q: What algebraic feature indicates orthogonality of two centred contrast spaces?

scenes.title: Orthogonality in Latin squares
scenes.objective: Explain treatment orthogonality to row and column effects.

blocks.body: Each treatment occurs exactly once in every row and exactly once in every column.
This balanced incidence makes treatment contrasts orthogonal to row contrasts and to column contrasts under the standard Latin-square model.
The row and column effects can be adjusted without confounding the treatment contrasts in the standard balanced layout.

ask.q: In a Latin square, treatment contrasts are orthogonal to which two effects?

scenes.title: Connectedness is not balance
scenes.problem: A design has a connected treatment concurrence graph, but some pairs occur together twice and others never occur together directly. Is it connected? Is it a BIBD?
hints: BIBD asks for equal pair concurrence.
Compute the target rank or compare the pair-concurrence condition before concluding.
scenes.answer: The design is connected but not a BIBD.
scenes.check: Connectedness and pair balance are different properties.

ask.q: Can a connected design fail to be a BIBD?
ask.nudge: Yes; paths need not give equal pair concurrence.

scenes.title: Connectedness and orthogonality traps
scenes.intro: Mark each statement TRUE or FALSE. The reasons distinguish estimability, balance and orthogonality.

items.claim: A connected design with v treatments has rank(C)=v−1.
items.why: All v−1 independent treatment contrasts are estimable.

items.claim: A path through intermediate treatments is enough for graph connectedness.
items.why: Every pair need not share a block directly.

items.claim: Connectedness and BIBD pair balance are the same property.
items.why: Connectedness concerns estimability; BIBD balance concerns equal pair concurrence.

items.claim: Orthogonality of centred contrast spaces is indicated by zero cross-products.
items.why: This is the algebraic definition of orthogonality.

scenes.title: Connectedness and orthogonality mastery
scenes.objective: Consolidate graph, rank and contrast ideas.
body: Connectedness means all treatment contrasts are estimable. Use the treatment concurrence graph or the rank condition rank(C)=v−1 for C=R−NK⁻¹N′. A path is enough; every pair need not share a block.

Orthogonality means centred contrast cross-products are zero. Complete RBD treatment contrasts are orthogonal to block contrasts; Latin-square treatment contrasts are orthogonal to row and column contrasts. Connectedness, balance and orthogonality are distinct.
